\ No newline at end of file === DIFF: docs/learning/lessons/0037-using-the-platform-user-guide.html === @@ -0,0 +1,273 @@ + + + + + +0037 — Using the Platform: The Operator's Guide + + + +
+

HFT Practice · Lesson 0037 · Operator's Guide

+

Using the Platform: From Fresh Clone to a Running Strategy Arena

+
Why this matters: the platform now has ~15 entry +points and a multi-stage workflow (train → validate → screen → live paper-trade → +monitor → decide). This is the map: what to run, in what order, and which safety +rails are watching you. Everything here is a real command from +pyproject.toml's [project.scripts].
+ +
Branch note: the arena commands +(arena-run and friends) live on the PR stack +#52 → #53 → #63. Until those merge to main, run them from +the feature/july6-batch branch.
+ +

1 · One-time setup

+
git clone https://github.com/bjl14710/algo_trading_practice.git
+cd algo_trading_practice
+uv sync --extra dev        # installs everything + pytest; NEVER bare pip
+uv run pytest tests/ -m "not exercise"   # sanity: should be all green
+

Environment variables (only needed for their feature): ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY +(news pipeline), WEB_AUTH_USER/PASS (web app), RH_USERNAME/PASSWORD/MFA +(Robinhood execution). Docker users: cp .env.docker.example .env.docker, fill it, +never commit it.

+ +

2 · The command map

+ + + + + + + + + + + + + +
CommandWhat it doesWhen you run it
paper-backtestTrains the GBM + historical backtest; --save_model writes the bundle (now with the drift reference baked in)When (re)training a model
walkforward-simRolling walk-forward with risk overlay; --stress replays COVID-2020 / 2022 / Q4-2018 shock windowsValidating a model before trusting it
arena-run backtestScreens strategies (engulfing, technical, meanrev, gbm) through one filter bar; stores PASS/EXCLUDED + sizing mode + divergence fingerprintOnce per strategy configuration
arena-run liveOne idempotent daily paper tick per PASS strategy — backfills missed days, evaluates breaker + divergenceDaily (cron or morning routine)
arena-run reportUnranked side-by-side table: live vs backtest, win rate, drawdown, alertsWhenever you want the standings
arena-run resume <name>The ONLY way to un-pause a breaker-tripped strategyAfter you've reviewed why it tripped
arena-run ensembleWeighted-vote meta-strategy from PASS members, weights = live SharpeOnce members have ~20 live days
predict-nextTomorrow's per-ticker predictions + allocation; --explain (SHAP), --check_drift (PSI)Ad-hoc, or via morning-runner
analyze-equitySharpe/CAGR/drawdown from any equity CSVAfter any backtest
web-hft / gui-hftFastAPI web app (:8000) / Tkinter desktop GUIBrowsing results visually
rh-execRobinhood order submission — dry-run by defaultOnly when you mean it
+ +

3 · The core workflow, end to end

+

Step A — Train a model (optional: rule strategies need no model)

+
uv run paper-backtest --tickers_file tickers/sap500_tickers.txt \
+    --start 2016-01-01 --end 2020-12-31 \
+    --save_model models/my_bundle.joblib
+

The bundle stores {"model", "features", "feature_reference"} — the +features list pins column order at inference (lesson 0035), the reference powers +drift checks (lesson 0036).

+ +

Step B — Validate it, including against crashes

+
uv run walkforward-sim --model models/my_bundle.joblib \
+    --start 2021-01-01 --end 2025-01-01 --stress
+uv run analyze-equity --equity_csv walkforward_equity.csv
+

--stress appends one metrics row per historical shock window — the +scenarios a few months of live paper trading will never show you.

+ +

Step C — Screen the arena field

+
uv run arena-run backtest --start 2023-01-01 --end 2025-01-01 \
+    --tickers AAPL,MSFT,GOOG,AMZN,NVDA \
+    --cost_model realistic          # net-of-costs screening
+# add gbm explicitly: --strategies engulfing,technical,meanrev,gbm --gbm_bundle models/my_bundle.joblib
+

Each strategy gets PASS or EXCLUDED against a lenient bar (Sharpe > 0, drawdown +< 30%) — excluded ones stay visible in the report, never silently dropped. The +sizing mode chosen here (conf_vol by default) is locked to the strategy's +ledger from now on.

+ +

Step D — Trade it live (paper), daily

+
uv run arena-run live      # ticks every PASS strategy
+

Idempotent: run it twice, nothing duplicates. Miss a week: it backfills +deterministically. Each tick also evaluates the drawdown breaker (auto-pause at +−20%) and the divergence z-test (flags likely overfits). Cron it or add it to your +morning routine next to morning-runner.

+ +

Step E — Read the standings, act like the human in the loop

+
uv run arena-run report
+

Key columns: status (PASS/EXCLUDED/PAUSED), sharpe_divergence +and divergence_z (overfit canaries), vol_ratio, +paused_since. A PAUSED strategy stays dark until +arena-run resume <name> — resuming resets its drawdown baseline to today.

+ +

Step F — When track records exist, try the ensemble

+
uv run arena-run ensemble --name blend --members engulfing,technical,meanrev
+ +

4 · The safety rails (what's protecting you)

+ + + + + + + + +
RailDefaultOverride
Real-money ordersrh-exec is dry-run--no_dry_run, typed by you, on purpose
Drawdown breakerPauses a live strategy at −20% from peak--breaker_dd / --no_breaker
Divergence alertFlags (never pauses) at z < −2 after 20 live days--divergence_z, --min_live_days
Regime gateReversal strategies sit out trending markets, momentum sits out mean-reverting ones--no_regime_gate
Position capNo single name above 30% of the book (conf_vol)--max_pos
Cost realismflat (legacy) so old numbers reproduce--cost_model realistic for honest nets
+ +

5 · Often confused with each other

+ + + + + + +
PairThe difference
paper-backtest vs walkforward-simpaper-backtest trains AND tests once (single split — optimistic); walkforward-sim never trains on the day it trades (rolling, honest). Validate with the second.
arena-run backtest vs arena-run liveSame deterministic engine, different role: backtest = one-shot screening over a fixed window; live = incremental daily ticks persisted to arena_state/arena.db with watchdogs active.
PAUSED vs EXCLUDEDEXCLUDED failed the screening backtest (never traded live); PAUSED was trading live until the breaker tripped it. Only PAUSED can be resumed.
predict-next vs arena-run livepredict-next is a one-off forecast + suggested allocation (nothing persisted); arena live maintains ongoing ledgers and track records.
+ +

6 · Practice

+

Score: 0 / 0

+ +
+

Q1. You retrained a model and want to trust it before the arena sees it. Which command sequence is right?

+
    +
  • paper-backtest → predict-next → arena-run live
    • +
  • paper-backtest --save_model → walkforward-sim --stress → arena-run backtest
    • +
  • paper-backtest --save_model → arena-run live
    • +
  • walkforward-sim → rh-exec → arena-run report
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q2. Your laptop was closed for four days. What do you do about the arena's missed ticks?

+
    +
  • Run arena-run live --backfill 4
    • +
  • Delete arena_state/arena.db and re-screen
    • +
  • Just run arena-run live — it backfills the gap automatically
    • +
  • INSERT the missing rows into the equity table by hand
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q3. The report shows meanrev: PAUSED, paused_since=2026-07-01. What happened, and what's the ONLY way it trades again?

+
    +
  • It failed the backtest filter; re-run arena-run backtest
    • +
  • Its live drawdown crossed the breaker threshold; arena-run resume meanrev after your review
    • +
  • The divergence z-test paused it; wait for z to recover
    • +
  • The regime gate paused it; it resumes when the regime flips
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q4. Which single flag moves you from "gross-ish" results to net-of-costs results across screening?

+
    +
  • --trade_cost_bps 5
    • +
  • --cost_model realistic
    • +
  • --max_pos 0.30
    • +
  • --fallback_adv 500000
    • +
+

+
+ +
+

Q5. What does it take for real money to move on this platform?

+
    +
  • A strategy passing arena-run backtest
    • +
  • Running predict-next with --capital set
    • +
  • You explicitly running rh-exec --no_dry_run
    • +
  • Building an ensemble of PASS strategies
    • +
+

+
+ +

7 · Check your understanding (scenarios)

+
Scenario A. Monday morning routine in three commands — what would yours be? +

Something like: arena-run live (tick + backfill the weekend, watchdogs run), +arena-run report (read the standings, note any PAUSED/diverged rows), +and predict-next --model ... --explain --check_drift if you want the GBM's +view of today with its reasoning and input-health attached. morning-runner +can wrap the pipeline pieces you automate.

+
Scenario B. The report shows technical's live Sharpe at 0.1 vs backtest 1.4, divergence_z = −2.6, but it's NOT paused. Why not, and what's your move? +

Divergence flags but never pauses — its drawdown hasn't breached the breaker. +The z-score says live returns are inconsistent with the screening backtest beyond +sampling noise: the classic overfit signature (lesson 0036). Your move is judgment: +check --check_drift-style input health and the regime log; if nothing +external explains it, retire or re-screen the strategy. The system deliberately +leaves that call to you.

+
Scenario C. You want the engulfing strategy to trade in ALL regimes for an experiment. Two ways to do it? +

Quick and global: --no_regime_gate on the arena command (disables gating +for every strategy that run). Surgical and permanent: widen +DailyEngulfingStrategy.compatible_regimes in +strategies/candlestick_daily.py — but that's a strategy-definition change, +so re-screen afterwards.

+ +
+ + + + + + +
+ + +
+ + Investigate per the method in your instructions, then return the findings list.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud (requires claude.ai account access)). Both changed files are static documentation HTML pages. Analyzing per the method:

**Phase 1 — Entry points & sinks:**
- `docs/learning/index.html`: Only diff is a count bump ("8 → 9") and one new `<div class="row">` linking to the new lesson. No script, no dynamic input.
- `docs/learning/lessons/0037-using-the-platform-user-guide.html`: New static lesson page. Only one small script that:
  - Uses `shuffle()` with `Math.random()` (quiz option randomization — not a security context)
  - Reads `dataset.correct` / `dataset.why` from **hardcoded literals** in the same file
  - Writes them via `textContent` (safe — no HTML parsing) and `classList.add()` with hardcoded strings
  - Sets `feedback.style.color` to a hardcoded var(--good)/var(--bad)

**Phase 2 — Data flow:**
- No attacker-influenceable source anywhere. All `data-*` attributes are author-controlled literals baked into the page. There is no query-string, `location.hash`, `postMessage`, `fetch`, storage, or cookie access.
- Sinks used (`textContent`, `classList.add`, `style.color` with a constant, `dataset` read) are either safe by construction or fed only constants.

**Phase 2c — High-miss patterns:**
- No logging/telemetry, no IaC, no CI/CD changes, no allowlists, no permission grants, no identity/DNS teardown, no validators, no gate/action mismatches, no resource caps, no shell/path/loader/URI sinks. The prose mentions env vars (`ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY`, `WEB_AUTH_USER/PASS`, `RH_USERNAME/PASSWORD/MFA`) and Robinhood dry-run defaults — that's documentation text, not code that reads or exposes them. No secrets are embedded (the only URL is the public GitHub repo).
- The `Math.random()` in `shuffle()` is quiz-answer ordering — no security decision depends on it.

**Phase 3:** No source→sink path exists in either file.

No vulnerabilities identified.
